faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person or beekeeper to keep any bee hive box or colony
               that is not in strict compliance with any provision of this article.
(1)
Hive boxes and supers.
(i)
All bee colonies shall be kept in a hive box with removable frames to facilitate inspection.
               All hive boxes, frames, and other equipment shall be kept in sound and usable condition.
(ii)
No hive box shall contain more than ten frames.
(iii)
No hive box shall have inside dimensions that exceed ten inches in height, 14 inches
               in width, or 19 inches in depth.
(iv)
No colony shall contain more than three hive boxes.
(v)
No colony shall contain more than four supers.
(vi)
All hive boxes must rest upon a hive box stand or other appropriate foundation structure.
(2)
Colony density.
(i)
The number of colonies allowed on a particular tract of land shall be determined by
               the size of the tract upon which the apiary is located. No beekeeper shall keep or
               possess more than the maximum number of colonies per tract as shown in Table 38-403.
TABLE 38-403
MAXIMUM NUMBER OF COLONIES
ALLOWED PER TRACT
SIZE OF TRACT
MAXIMUM NUMBER OF COLONIES ALLOWED
One-quarter acre or less.
Two colonies.
More than one-quarter acre up to and including one-half acre.
Four colonies.
More than one-half acre up to and including one acre.
Six colonies.
More than one acre.
Eight colonies.
Exception:
Regardless of tract size, where all hive boxes are situated at least 200 feet in
                  every direction from all property lines of the tract on which the apiary is located,
                  there shall be no limit to the number of colonies which may be located thereon.
(ii)
For each two colonies authorized under colony densities set forth in
section 38-403
(a)(2)(i) above, there may be maintained upon the same tract one nucleus colony in
                     a hive box containing no more than ten frames with no supers and with inside hive
                     box dimensions not exceeding those set forth in
section 38-403
(a)(1)(iii) above. The nucleus colony shall be disposed of or combined with an authorized
                     colony within 30 days after the date it was acquired.
(3)
Setback.
(i)
No hive box, except an observation hive, shall be located within 25 feet from any
                  adjoining property as measured from the nearest point on the hive box to the adjoining
                  property line, with the back of the hive box facing the nearest adjoining property.
(ii)
No hive box shall be located in any front setback.
(4)
Junk and debris surrounding the apiary site. Each beekeeper shall ensure that the
                  area surrounding the apiary site is kept neat and in good order. Each beekeeper shall
                  ensure that no bee honeycomb, brood comb, or other hive box materials are left upon
                  the grounds of the apiary site. Upon their removal from the hive box, all such materials
                  shall be promptly disposed of in a sealed container or placed within an enclosed building
                  or other bee-proof enclosure.
(5)
Observation hive. In addition to the colony densities set forth in
section 38-403
(a)(2) above, a beekeeper may keep or maintain no more than four observation hives
                  upon any property. All observation hives that contain bees or brood shall be located
                  within an enclosed building used or occupied by humans.
Exception:
No beekeeper may keep or maintain more than one observation hive on any property
                  zoned as residential.
(
Ord. No. 4345, § 1, 8-6-2012
)
